content.value_statement: DeFi teams need repeatable smart contract starting points. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code templates for staking, AMMs, governance, lending, and flash loans.
actual_capabilities: Provides Solidity templates for staking rewards and token withdrawals.
Outlines AMM liquidity, share minting, swaps, and reserve updates.
Includes governance token and proposal voting patterns.
Shows a flash loan provider and receiver flow.
Lists DeFi implementation resources and security best practices.
limitations: It does not replace a professional smart contract audit.
Examples require adaptation to token standards, oracles, and protocol economics.
It does not include tests, deployment scripts, or formal verification artifacts.
It does not verify live protocol parameters or market risks.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a Protocol MVP
use_cases.description: Start from staking, AMM, governance, lending, or flash loan templates before adding project requirements.

use_cases.title: Compare DeFi Building Blocks
use_cases.description: Review common protocol patterns before selecting an architecture for a new product.

use_cases.title: Plan Security Reviews
use_cases.description: Use the templates to identify assumptions, external calls, and audit checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the right DeFi protocol template for my project. My goal is [goal], my token type is [token], and my main user action is [action].

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Staking Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staking rewards design using this skill. Include reward timing, withdrawal rules, admin controls, and security checks for [token name].

prompt_templates.title: Review an AMM Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AMM design against the template. Check liquidity minting, swap math, reserve updates, fee handling, and slippage assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Audit Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a security review plan for a DeFi protocol based on these templates. Cover threat models, tests, invariants, and audit questions.

output_examples.input: Design a staking rewards contract for a governance token.
output: A staking flow with deposits, withdrawals, reward accounting, and claim steps.
A list of access controls, reentrancy protections, and audit questions.
A testing checklist for reward math, edge cases, and emergency behavior.

output_examples.input: Compare AMM and lending templates for a new DeFi product.
output: A side-by-side comparison of liquidity needs, risk exposure, and user actions.
Recommended starting template based on product goals and operational constraints.
Open questions about oracle design, collateral rules, and market assumptions.

output_examples.input: Prepare a flash loan integration review.
output: A review checklist for callbacks, repayment checks, fees, and receiver validation.
Threat scenarios covering failed repayment, malicious receivers, and external calls.
Suggested tests for liquidity limits, fee rounding, and transaction rollback.

best_practices: Treat templates as starting points and document every protocol-specific assumption.
Add unit tests, fuzz tests, invariant tests, and deployment checks before launch.
Use reviewed libraries and schedule an independent audit for production contracts.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy generated contracts without tests, audits, and parameter review.
Do not copy financial logic without adapting token decimals, fees, and oracle assumptions.
Do not ignore external call risks, admin powers, or emergency controls.

faq.question: What protocols does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers staking rewards, AMMs, governance tokens, lending concepts, and flash loan flows.

faq.question: Can I deploy the templates directly?
faq.answer: No. Treat them as starting points that need tests, review, and a professional audit.

faq.question: Does it include complete project scaffolding?
faq.answer: No. The skill provides templates and guidance, not full test suites or deployment tooling.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Is this useful for security reviewers?
faq.answer: Yes. Reviewers can use the examples to identify assumptions and build audit checklists.

faq.question: Does it handle live protocol risk?
faq.answer: No. You must evaluate market risk, governance risk, oracle risk, and operational controls separately.
